transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop thinking about how old and wrong my face looks, and it’s getting in the way of me moving up at work. A nurse I trust suggested I come speak with someone because it's starting to really affect my career.
Do you spend most of your time worrying that other people are judging your appearance, or do you worry about many different things in life such as work, money, health, and family?

Almost all of my worry is focused on my face—specifically how old and wrong it looks and how people at work will judge me for it. I don't really have those constant worries about things like money, health, or family; it is almost entirely about my appearance and how it's holding me back.
When you worry about your face, do you also spend a lot of time checking mirrors, comparing your appearance to others, or trying to hide or fix the way you look?

Yes, it's really embarrassing, but I spend 20 to 30 minutes in the mirror before work tilting my head, pulling my skin back, and trying different makeup and lighting. I also take and delete dozens of selfies to check how I'll look on camera, and I constantly ask my husband if I look too old.
Do you believe there is actually something wrong with your face that others can clearly see, or do you think the worry may be exaggerated?

To me, it feels completely real and obvious that my face is sagging and looks wrong, especially around my mouth and eyes, even though my husband and clients try to reassure me. I truly believe it looks that way, and I'm terrified my coworkers and boss will see it and think I'm just too worn out to be taken seriously as a leader.
Have you ever been able to consider that your face might actually look normal, or are you completely certain that it is truly deformed or wrong despite what others tell you?

Even though my husband and long-term clients constantly reassure me that I look fine, it is incredibly difficult to believe them. When I look in the mirror, I am completely convinced that my face looks aged, sagging, and just wrong. I find it almost impossible to see it any other way, no matter what they say.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs, such as feeling that people are spying on you, talking about you, or trying to harm you, outside of concerns about your appearance?

No, I have never felt like anyone is spying on me, trying to harm me, or talking about me in that way. My worries are strictly focused on how aged and wrong my face looks, and nothing else like that has ever crossed my mind.
Have you ever thought your face was actually being changed or damaged by an outside force, or is your concern only that it looks unattractive or aged to you and others?

No, I've never thought any outside force was changing or damaging my face. My concern is strictly that it looks too old, sagging, and worn out to me and others, which makes me feel like no one will take me seriously as a leader at work.
Do you think your face is truly deformed or damaged, or could it be that the way it looks is being exaggerated in your mind?

When I look in the mirror, the sagging and deep lines feel completely real and obvious, as if my face has just collapsed. Even though my husband and clients reassure me, it is incredibly hard to believe them because what I see is so distressing. It really doesn't feel like an exaggeration to me at all.

Have you ever considered that your face might actually look normal and that this concern could be exaggerated, or are you completely certain that it is truly deformed or wrong despite what others tell you?

While my husband and clients constantly reassure me that I look fine, I find it incredibly difficult to believe them. When I look in the mirror, the sagging and deep lines look so real and obvious that I am convinced my face looks wrong and too worn out. It is just really hard for me to see it any other way, no matter what they tell me.
Have you ever thought that this facial problem might not be real and could be just a worry or exaggeration, or are you completely certain that your face is truly deformed?
I'm not really sure anymore. Deep down it feels completely real and obvious to me, but sometimes I do wonder why everyone else seems to see something different.

When you think about your face, do you ever recognize that the concern might be a false belief or a symptom of an illness, or do you feel completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others say?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, because I've never thought of this as a false belief or an illness. All I know is that when I look in the mirror, the flaws feel completely real and incredibly distressing to me. It is just very hard for me to see it any other way.
When you worry about your face, do you ever think there is a chance your belief could be wrong, or are you completely certain that your face is truly deformed or damaged despite what others say?

I'm not quite sure how to answer that. While I hear the reassurances from my husband and others, it feels incredibly real to me when I look in the mirror, and I haven't really thought about whether I could be completely wrong.
Do you ever think your concern about your face might be a symptom of a mental health condition or an overreaction, or are you completely convinced that your face is truly deformed or wrong?

I'm here because a nurse I trust urged me to seek help and I know this is hurting my career, but it's still so hard to believe it's just a mental health issue or an overreaction. When I look in the mirror, the deep lines and sagging look completely real and undeniable, and I truly feel no one will take me seriously as a leader looking this worn out.
Have you had any other experiences where you were sure something strange or false was happening, such as believing people were spying on you, talking about you, or trying to harm you?
No, I have never had any experiences like that at all. I have never felt like people were spying on me, trying to harm me, or anything of that nature.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, like hearing or seeing things that others do not, or feeling that people are watching, talking about, or trying to harm you?

No, I've never heard or seen things that aren't there, and I don't feel paranoid or like anyone is trying to harm me. My concerns are strictly focused on my appearance and how it's impacting my career.

Do you think your concern about your face could be a false belief or a symptom of a mental health condition, or are you completely certain that your face is truly deformed or wrong despite what others say?

I honestly don't know if this is a mental health issue or just reality, and it's very confusing to think about. To me, the flaws on my face feel completely real and are so hard to ignore, even though I am here seeking help.

Have you ever had a period when you were completely convinced that your face was deformed or damaged and could not be persuaded otherwise, even for a while? Or do you usually have at least some doubt that it might be your mind making it seem worse than it is?

I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms. For the most part, the worry just feels very constant and real to me. I don't know if I've had distinct periods of doubt or absolute certainty; it's just always been a struggle.

When you think about your face, do you ever recognize that this concern might be a symptom of a mental health condition or an overreaction, or are you completely convinced that your face is truly deformed or wrong despite what others say?
I'm not really sure. To me, my face genuinely looks wrong and too aged, but since a nurse I trust suggested I get help, I am trying to be open to the possibility that I might be overreacting.
When you think about your face, do you feel completely certain it is truly deformed or damaged, or can you recognize that this might be a false belief or an overreaction at least sometimes?

I'm not really sure how to answer that because even though my husband tells me it's not that bad, when I look in the mirror, I feel completely convinced that my face looks terribly aged and wrong. It is just so hard to shake that feeling, even for a second, because what I see looks so real.
When you think about your face, do you ever realize that the belief might be exaggerated or untrue, or are you completely convinced it is really deformed even when others disagree?

It's hard to say. Even though others disagree, when I look in the mirror, I am completely convinced that my face looks aged and wrong. That makes it feel very real to me, no matter what anyone else says.
When you look at your face, do you ever think there is a real chance you might be mistaken, or are you completely certain that it is truly deformed or damaged despite what others say?

While my husband and long-term clients constantly reassure me that I look fine, it is incredibly difficult to believe them. When I look in the mirror, the deep lines and sagging around my mouth and eyes look so undeniably real and "wrong" that I feel almost completely certain of it. Even so, a small part of me keeps asking my husband for reassurance, hoping to be proven wrong.
Besides your concern about your face, have you ever had other fixed beliefs that others thought were untrue, such as being watched, followed, talked about, or harmed?
No, I have never experienced any of those kinds of thoughts or beliefs about being watched or followed. My concern is strictly focused on how old and wrong my face looks.
Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that other people said were untrue, such as being watched, followed, talked about, or harmed?

No, I have never had any other beliefs like that, and I've never felt watched, followed, or harmed by anyone. My concerns are strictly focused on how aged my face looks and how it's getting in the way of my career.
When you think about your face, can you recognize that this may be a false or exaggerated belief, or are you completely convinced it is truly deformed despite what others say?

Although my husband and long-term clients reassure me that I look fine, I really struggle to believe them. When I look in the mirror, I am deeply convinced that my face looks sagging, collapsed, and worn out, and it feels entirely real to me. Even though I try to seek reassurance, the conviction that my face looks "wrong" and too old is just overwhelming.
Outside of your concerns about your face, have you ever had other fixed beliefs that other people thought were untrue, such as being watched, followed, talked about, or harmed?
No, I have never had any beliefs like that, and I've never felt watched, followed, or harmed. My concerns are strictly focused on how my face looks.
Outside of your concern about your face, have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that other people thought were untrue, such as being watched, followed, talked about, or harmed?
No, I have never experienced anything like being followed, watched, or harmed. My main concern is strictly about how my face looks and how it is affecting my career.
When you think about your face, do you ever recognize that this concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or are you completely certain it is deformed despite what others say?

I am honestly torn about it. Part of me hopes that I am just exaggerating because of the stress at work, but whenever I look in the mirror, the sagging and deep lines feel completely real and hard to ignore.
When you look in the mirror, do you ever think your concern about your face might be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others say?

When I look in the mirror, the sagging and deep lines feel completely real and undeniable to me, like my face has collapsed and looks totally "wrong." I ask my husband for reassurance repeatedly because I desperately want to be wrong, but in those moments I feel completely certain of what I'm seeing. That makes it incredibly hard to believe anyone else's reassurance.
Have you ever had any other unusual experiences or beliefs, like hearing voices, feeling watched or followed, or believing people are trying to harm you, outside of your concerns about your face?
No, I have never heard voices, felt watched, or believed anyone was trying to harm me. My concerns are strictly focused on my face and how my appearance is affecting my career.

Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs or unusual experiences outside of your appearance concern, such as feeling watched, followed, talked about, or harmed, or hearing or seeing things others do not?
No, I have never had any experiences like that, and I've never heard or seen things that weren't there. My worries are strictly and completely focused on how old and wrong my face looks.
